subject: Active-Passive Coexistence Validation & SLA Runbook — follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Gates <alex.gates@acme-fin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-fin.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Active-passive coexistence validation + runbook request

Jonas —

Thanks for the talk yesterday. As part of our RFP we need a tightly scoped response on how Redwood supports an active-passive deployment across two US regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary) with emphasis on: RTO/RPO guarantees for inference endpoints, behavior during automated failover, how cached KV/session state is handled, and the expected functional and performance impact during the first 60/90 minutes after failover (cache warm-up).

Specifically, can you provide the following in a concise runbook or matrix we can include in our procurement packet:
- Formal RTO and RPO commitments (and any conditionality) for production inference requests
- Sequence of automated actions during a regional switchover and expected per-step timings
- Known limitations (e.g., session affinity, in-flight request behaviors, degraded throughput windows)
- Recommended rehearsal cadence and evidence we can request after a drill (logs, perf graphs, canary results)
- A short excerpt of the runbook that we can circulate to our ops team (2–3 pages)

One more ask: our security team wants to understand whether Redwood can accept an SLA exception for a one-time rehearsal where full cache restoration may push effective service recovery beyond your standard SLA window (we typically plan for a 90-minute warm-up window for the first cross-region rehearsal). If that is feasible, please include how that exception would be documented and what compensating controls (observability, rollback) you will provide.

Appreciate a response with attachments and a 1–2 line summary we can pass to legal/procurement this week.

Regards,
Alex Gates
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Acme Financial Services

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gates <alex.gates@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Active-passive coexistence validation + runbook request

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts we prepared specifically for your procurement packet: (1) active-passive-validation-matrix.xlsx — a compact table that maps failure modes to system actions and expected timings, and (2) runbook-extract.md — a 3-page excerpt you can share with operations. Both are summarized below.

High-level summary (for legal/procurement):
- RTO (service endpoint recovery): 2 minutes for automated routing/failover to the secondary region for stateless inference requests.
- RPO (data loss): near-zero for persistent metadata and customer-managed artifacts replicated via geo-replication. For ephemeral KV caches (per-request context cache), expected RPO is tied to your session persistence settings; typical recovery means the secondary will resume with no guaranteed per-request context for in-flight sessions — this is mitigated with prefix caching and client-side checkpoints.
- First-failure warm-up: during the first cross-region rehearsal, throughput to match steady-state may require 30–90 minutes of cache warm-up depending on model size and traffic profile. We can quantify this for your specific model set during a pre-rehearsal profiling run.
- Degraded behaviors: short-term higher-latency tail, adaptive batching reduced efficiency, and increased GPU cold-starts for large models. We document fallback behaviors (automatic model shedding to smaller quantized variants) in the runbook extract.

SLA exception: we can accommodate a documented one-time SLA exception for the initial rehearsal (up to 90 minutes additional recovery window) provided: (a) the rehearsal is scheduled in advance, (b) Redwood operates under a documented rollback plan and live observability hooks for Acme, and (c) Acme acknowledges the exception in procurement paperwork. The attachment includes a suggested exception form that your procurement/legal team can sign.

Next steps we propose:
- Schedule a 60-min profiling call to capture model sizes and traffic shape (I can run the profiler within 48 hours)
- Confirm a rehearsal week (we prefer a weekday maintenance window)
- Redwood to provide pre-rehearsal checklist and sample log artifacts after the drill

I’m happy to walk the ops team through the attached runbook extract — suggest Wed or Thu next week.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: active-passive-validation-matrix.xlsx, runbook-extract.md

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Active-passive coexistence validation + runbook request — SLA exception request

Team —

Looping you in. Acme asks for a one-time SLA exception (up to 90 minutes of additional recovery time) for their initial cross-region rehearsal because of expected cache warm-up. I indicated that we can honor this with the following controls:
- Signed exception form and rehearsal schedule (attached in the runbook extract)
- Redwood will provide live observability (per-route latency/cost charts, canary traces) and a rollback plan that can be triggered by either side
- We will provide artifacts post-rehearsal: perf graphs, canary success/failure list, and a short executive summary for Acme security.

Please advise: do we need Product/Ops sign-off for the exception or can we approve this from Solutions/Sales? Also confirm whether Support should create an internal postmortem template for the rehearsal.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments — that matrix is exactly the format our procurement team wants. We reviewed the runbook extract with Security Ops; the SLA exception approach looks acceptable provided Redwood will supply the post-rehearsal observability bundle and the canary traces you mentioned.

Action items we agreed internally:
- Acme to sign the exception form and confirm rehearsal window by end of next week
- Redwood to run the profiling job and return model-specific warm-up estimate within 48 hours
- Joint 60-min rehearsal plan call (ops + security) — proposed Thu 04 Jun 2026 11:00 PT

Please confirm the call time and attach the pre-rehearsal checklist so we can circulate it to our runbook owners.

Regards,
Alex Gates
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Acme Financial Services
